why_prevention: the slot is reserved in an in-memory count before send_chat is called, so the decision no longer depends on the writer having flushed; rows are read from disk only once, at run start

evidence.command_or_count: GREEN: brake restored -> rc=4 rows=0 requests=0
evidence.zero_rows_on_refusal: cap=100 spent=100 headroom=100 -> CAP REFUSED at T1, rc=4, rows=0, transport calls=0; arithmetic printed with spent/would_spend/cap/reserve/headroom/allocation/used_in_run/turn
evidence.midrun_stop_turn: allocation=2 on a 3-turn cell -> CAP REFUSED at T3; rows written = [(T1,turn),(T2,turn)]; used_in_run=2; manifest final_used_in_run=2
evidence.followup_counting: allocation=1 on a tool-call turn -> turn sent, follow-up REFUSED (kind=tool-followup), rc=4, rows=[turn], used_in_run=1; allocation=2 -> 2 requests, rc=0, final_used_in_run=2
evidence.allows: rc=0, used_in_run=2 == 2 rows, spent_at_start=10 spent_after=12 delta=0; manifest records allocation and final count
evidence.red_green: RED (pre-send call neutered): rc=9 rows=3 requests=3, first row T1/turn; GREEN (restored): rc=4 rows=0 requests=0
evidence.reconcile: delta>0 (a row no request bought) -> exit 9 'CAP GATE RECONCILE DIVERGENCE (delta=+1)'; delta<0 (request stranded mid-turn) -> loud 'CAP GATE UNRECORDED ... reported, never silent'
evidence.exit_codes: subprocess: refusal -> process exit 4; bad --request-allocation -> 3; unparseable row file -> 5 (all before any send)
evidence.tool_channel2: assertion (e) drifted:     assert filtered["before"] == filtered["after"], (filtered, "tools-off output drifted")

known_limit: a refusal that lands MID-turn can strand the rows of follow-ups already obtained in that turn (the turn's own row is flushed before stopping); the stranded count is printed as CAP GATE UNRECORDED and the next run's disk read under-counts by exactly that many. Reported, never silent.
next_unit_hint: WIRE-GATES (444654f4) joins the preflight chain; do not fold this loop brake into cell.py. --budget-glob lets a cell isolate its scan set.
assumptions: --request-allocation default 'projection' equals the cell's existing structural request count (turns + digests + fetch-round pool), so the in-memory brake and the pre-existing 'sent >= budget' abort cannot disagree about the ceiling
the gate scans measure/rows-*.jsonl by default; the run's own row file is added when it exists, so the exit reconciliation sees this run's rows
a row file that does not exist yet is zero rows, not an unreadable file (exit 5 stays reserved for unreadable/unparseable)
